title: Reefer Cargo Services: Number of Services per Customer and per Container
content:
Reefer Cargo Services is ordered container by container, and this page states how many services may coexist. There is no ceiling at the level of the customer: a shipper or forwarder may hold any number of reefer services at once, whatever the number of bookings or containers involved.

## Clause

The limit sits at the level of the container within a booking. A given reefer container on a given booking may have at most one live service. Every status a service can hold counts as live except cancelled, so a service that is requested, inspection passed, plugged in, in transit, delivered or closed occupies that container on that booking. The question is settled from the line's own service records for the booking and container concerned, read as they stand when the new order is about to be placed; a caller's recollection of earlier orders does not stand in for that record.

## Input, judgement and outcome

| Services already on record for the same booking and the same container | Does the one-live-service limit stand in the way of another order? |
|---|---|
| none | no |
| cancelled services only | no |
| a service in any status other than cancelled | yes |

The limit is only one of the tests an order must meet; a "no" in the right-hand column means this limit raises no objection, not that the order is admitted.

## Hypothetical cases

- A forwarder already holds sixty reefer services spread over many bookings. Nothing in this page restricts a further order for a container that has no live service on its booking.
- A container's service on a booking was cancelled before inspection. A new order for the same container on the same booking is not blocked by this limit, because a cancelled service is not live.
- A container's service on a booking was delivered and its file closed. That closed service is still live for this purpose, so a second service for the same container on the same booking is blocked.
- The same container number appears on two different bookings. Each booking and container pair is assessed separately, so a live service on one booking does not occupy the container on the other.
